45 CFR 170.315 Offers Buyers a MedGemma Validation Checklist: Google’s model card and ONC’s certified-health-IT rule point to the same buyer questions: intended use, local evidence, monitoring, and ownership. Image created by the author with diffusion-synthesis and Python post-processing.Google’s MedGemma 1.5 model card can look harmless beside a clean chest X-ray demo, but the hospital’s risk is already open in the next tab. Once an innovation lead approves a pilot without writing down who owns validation, override, monitoring, and shutdown, a vendor promise becomes an operational risk for the unit.
This is for hospital innovation leads, clinical AI product owners, and founders selling decision-support pilots into regulated care. The proof object is a cross-read between Google’s MedGemma 1.5 model card and current 45 CFR 170.315(b)(11). This is a comparison, not a claim that MedGemma itself is regulated by that section: Google supplies a developer limitation, while the federal section supplies a certification criterion for Health IT Modules. The procurement value is the checklist, not a newly invented legal duty.
The Model Card Is the First Transfer
